issues.legal_issue: Additional compensation for acquired land does not accrue for a period before publication of the acquisition notification, even when possession was taken earlier.
material_facts: Possession of the owners’ land was taken for an irrigation project before publication of the acquisition notification.
The acquisition notification was published later, followed by an award of compensation.
In execution proceedings, the owners claimed additional compensation beginning on the earlier date when possession was taken.
issues.conclusion: The owners were entitled to additional compensation only for the period beginning on publication of the acquisition notification and ending on the date of the award, because possession had been taken before the notification.
issues.legal_principle: Section 23(1A) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 fixes the beginning of the additional-compensation period at publication of the notification under Section 4(1), and its endpoint at the award or taking of possession, whichever is earlier. Where possession precedes publication, that possession date cannot serve as the endpoint for a period beginning at publication; the award is the available endpoint. The provision’s clear language permits no alternative construction to avoid an allegedly unjust result. The Court approved Special Tahsildar (LA), P.W.D. Schemes v. M.A. Jabbar, [1995] 2 SCC 142, and disapproved Asstt. Commr., Gadag Sub-Division v. Mathapathi Basavannewwa, [1995] 6 SCC 355, and State of H.P. v. Dharam Das, [1995] 5 SCC 683.

predicates.additional_compensation_claim_in_land_ac: The proceeding concerns a claim for additional compensation in a land acquisition.
predicates.possession_precedes_notice_publication: The acquiring authority took possession of the land before the acquisition notice was published.
predicates.award_follows_notice_publication: The compensation award was made after publication of the acquisition notice.

issues.definition: When a claim for additional compensation in a land acquisition involves possession before notice publication and an award after publication, the earlier possession does not extend the additional-compensation period to before publication.
